questions.learningObjective: Apply the product rule to two cost factors
questions.stem: Explain why the product rule gives (uv)'=u'v+uv' for two ingredient cost factors u(x) and v(x).

answer.exemplar: The product rule follows from the limit definition: (uv)'=lim[(u(x+h)v(x+h)-u(x)v(x))/h], splitting into u'v+uv' by adding and subtracting u(x)v(x+h). This captures both factors changing simultaneously.

questions.explanation: The product rule accounts for changes in both factors. The tempting wrong idea is that the derivative of a product is just the product of derivatives.
questions.hint: Consider how both u and v change over a small interval.

questions.learningObjective: Compute derivative of a square root via limit
questions.stem: Explain the derivative of f(x)=sqrt(x) using the power rule.

answer.exemplar: Rewrite sqrt(x)=x^{1/2}. By power rule, f'(x)=(1/2)x^{-1/2}=1/(2 sqrt(x)). This gives the instantaneous rate of change.

questions.explanation: Power rule with exponent 1/2 yields 1/(2 sqrt(x)). The tempting wrong idea is to treat sqrt as linear.
questions.hint: Use exponent 1/2 and power rule.
